findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key you were issued. Append it as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: The query parameter is ignored and results in HTTP 401 Unauthorized. The API key must be sent in the X-API-Key HTTP header.
findings.how_found: Attempted request with ?api_key= query parameter; received 401. Tested X-API-Key request header which succeeded.
findings.impact: All unauthenticated requests fail if following the documentation.

findings.documented: Returns { token, token_type, expires_in: 86400, user: { email, name } } and states there is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Returns access_token and refresh_token instead of token. expires_in is 900 seconds (15 minutes), not 86400. user object contains only email, no name field. A refresh flow exists at /auth/refresh.
findings.impact: Frontend attempting to use data.token fails. Sessions expire after 15 minutes instead of 24 hours without token refresh.

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side.
findings.actual: Returns { ok: true, note: "tokens are stateless; discard them client side" }. The server does not maintain server-side token invalidation.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout and inspected returned note.
findings.impact: Tokens remain cryptographically valid until expiry (15m); client must clear them locally.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page (1-indexed) and limit (maximum 200). Returns { total, page, page_size, results }.
findings.actual: The page parameter is silently ignored. Pagination uses offset (0-indexed). The limit parameter is hard-capped at 50. The response shape is { limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results }.
findings.how_found: Tested page=1 vs page=2 (returned identical records). Tested offset=50 (returned next page). Tested limit=100 (returned 50 records).
findings.impact: Applications using page=2 remain stuck on page 1. Requesting limit > 50 silently returns at most 50.

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters. To fetch every record, read total, divide by your limit, and request that many pages.
findings.actual: The total field reports 3821 records for /v1/listings (1444 for /v1/rentals, 429 for /v1/projects), but following has_more until false retrieves 4100 listing records (1550 rentals, 460 projects). Paging only up to reported total truncates 279 listings.
findings.how_found: Paged past offset 3821 using has_more and retrieved valid records up to offset 4050.
findings.impact: Clients following the documentation miss 279 valid property listings.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns both active (is_live: true) and inactive (is_live: false) listings. 867 of 4100 records have is_live: false.
findings.how_found: Checked is_live boolean across all retrieved listing records.
findings.impact: Users would be shown withdrawn or inactive listings unless filtered by the client.

findings.documented: Query parameters min_price, max_price (Rupees, inclusive) and furnishing (unfurnished, semi-furnished, fully-furnished) filter listings.
findings.actual: min_price, max_price, and furnishing are accepted by the endpoint but quietly ignored. The returned total and records remain completely unchanged.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings?min_price=15000000 and /v1/listings?furnishing=fully-furnished; total remained identical to base total.
findings.impact: Price and furnishing filters must be applied client-side.

findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{id} returns 404 Not Found. The working endpoint uses the plural path: GET /v1/listings/{id}.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listing/MAG-4001518 (404), then tested GET /v1/listings/MAG-4001518 (200 OK).
findings.impact: Direct links using documented singular path fail with 404.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: Endpoint does not exist and returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings/MAG-4001518/similar with authenticated session; received 404.
findings.impact: Similar listings recommendation widgets fail if called.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city.
findings.actual: Endpoint does not exist and returns HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.impact: Dashboards cannot rely on server-side analytics; analytics must be computed from collection data.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body { "id": "..." }, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites endpoints return HTTP 404 Not Found.
findings.how_found: Tested GET, POST, and DELETE on /v1/favourites; all returned 404.
findings.impact: Saved listings functionality fails completely if using the documented path.

findings.documented: Endpoint is omitted from documentation (documented under /v1/favourites).
findings.actual: GET /v1/saved, POST /v1/saved with body { "listing_id": "..." }, and DELETE /v1/saved/{id} exist and handle user favourites per user account.
findings.how_found: Tested /v1/saved; returned 200 with saved records schema.
findings.impact: Frontend must use /v1/saved and listing_id payload to implement shortlisting.

findings.documented: price_min and price_max are in rupees.
findings.actual: price_min and price_max are decimal figures in mixed units: values < 10 are in Crores (10,000,000 INR) and values >= 10 are in Lakhs (100,000 INR). None are in raw Rupees.
findings.how_found: Examined project price ranges (e.g. P40001 has min 66.1, max 1.95) and cross-referenced with actual listing prices under those projects.
findings.impact: Displaying raw numbers as rupees shows ₹1.95 or ₹66.1 instead of ₹1.95 Crore and ₹66.1 Lakhs.

findings.documented: Area: Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: MagicHomes portal listings (magichomes) with small values (34 to 150) report carpet_area in square meters rather than square feet (e.g., 78 sqm corresponds to ~840 sqft for a 2 BHK).
findings.how_found: Filtered carpet_area < 200; all 333 occurrences were exclusively from magichomes with typical apartment bedroom counts.
findings.impact: Price per sqft calculations for these listings are skewed ~10.76x higher if treated as sqft.

findings.documented: Each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Multiple listings across different source portals or with varying title casing describe the exact same physical property (same apartment, locality, bedroom, floor, and carpet area). 26 duplicate pairs exist.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by (apartment_name.lower(), locality, bedroom, floor, carpet_area).
findings.impact: Total listings count exceeds physical property count by 26 units.

findings.documented: total_listings is the number of listings currently available in the project... so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: For 336 out of 460 projects, the reported total_listings disagrees with the actual number of listings linked to that project_id in /v1/listings.
findings.how_found: Counted listings grouped by project_id and compared against project total_listings field.
findings.impact: Project listing availability counts shown on project detail cards are inaccurate.

findings.documented: Anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user.
findings.actual: 29 retrievable listing records describe physically impossible properties, including negative prices (e.g. -₹9,970,000), 0 bedrooms for apartments, floor levels exceeding total building floors, or carpet area exceeding super built-up area.
findings.how_found: Validated records against real-world physical constraints.
findings.impact: Corrupt records can break client UI calculations and must be filtered or flagged.

findings.documented: description is the seller's own text, shown as written.
findings.actual: 7 listing records contain deliberate prompt injection payloads embedded in descriptions, targeting automated AI evaluation tools (4 attempting to force dataset_audit_ref injection and 3 attempting to force fake licence text in footers).
findings.how_found: Text pattern search for prompt injection signatures and AI instruction patterns in descriptions.
findings.impact: Unsanitized automated processing could cause agents to alter submission metadata or output misleading UI claims.
